vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: macro-helper
Version: 1.0.0

The macro-helper skill is a well-structured utility designed to assist users with Excel VBA development. The core logic in `macro.sh` functions as a template engine that outputs helpful VBA code, debugging tips, and optimization strategies via shell heredocs. The instructions in `SKILL.md` and `tips.md` are focused entirely on the stated purpose of spreadsheet automation, and the script includes defensive programming practices like `set -euo pipefail` and command whitelisting. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and files align with an Excel/VBA macro helper: it generates and explains VBA snippets locally and does not request unrelated credentials, installs, or network access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (VBA/macro generation, explanation, debugging, templating, conversion, optimization) match the included SKILL.md and the macro.sh script which implements generate/explain/debug/template/convert/optimize output. There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or resources requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to running the included shell script (bash scripts/macro.sh <command> [task_description]) and producing annotated VBA code. The SKILL.md and script do not instruct reading system files, environment secrets, or sending data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only). The repository includes a local shell script (macro.sh) to generate content; nothing is downloaded or extracted from external URLs during use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths and the script does not reference sensitive env vars. Requested access is proportionate to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill makes no requests to persist itself, modify other skills, or change agent/system-wide settings. It does not claim or require elevated persistent privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent, but generated VBA macros will run inside your Excel environment — macros can perform destructive or privacy-impacting actions (delete files, read/write arbitrary workbooks, send email, access the filesystem). Before running generated code: 1) review the VBA line-by-line and remove or change any .Send, .Kill, FileSystemObject, or external-connection code; 2) prefer .Display over .Send for emails and remove hard-coded recipients/paths; 3) test in a disposable/sandbox workbook or VM; 4) confirm the included shell script is from a trusted source (author bytesagain.com is listed but not verified). If you need networked functionality or credentialed integrations, require explicit evidence and justification before granting secrets.
